1-1.title: Write down recent challenges on sticky notes.
1-1.description: Small things that bother you count too. Write down whatever comes to mind.
1-1.illustrationAlt: Three sticky notes with everyday challenges

1-1.title: Write one challenge on each note.
1-1.description: Enter one challenge in the note composer and press Enter to add it. Use a new note when the topic changes.
1-1.illustrationAlt: Entering text in the note composer and adding a sticky note

1-1.title: Write down as many challenges as you can before time runs out.
1-1.description: While the timer is running, keep adding sticky notes with anything that comes to mind.

1-2.title: Share your notes and learn what everyone thinks.
1-2.description: Take turns explaining your thoughts and gather ideas to work on as a team.
1-2.illustrationAlt: Team members sharing their sticky notes

1-2.title: Present when it is your turn, then hand over to the next person.
1-2.description: Check the presenter shown at the top of the screen. When it is your turn, drag your private notes onto the board and explain them. Select “Done!” when you finish to pass the turn.
1-2.illustrationAlt: Waiting for the previous presenter, sharing a note on your turn, then selecting Done

1-3.title: Group similar challenges together.
1-3.description: Find common themes so the team can see the challenges at a glance.

1-3.title: Move similar notes close to each other.
1-3.description: Move notes into groups. Votes are cast on each individual note, not on a group.
1-3.illustrationAlt: Moving similar notes together into a group

1-4.title: Vote for the notes you want to work on.
1-4.description: Use the two sticker types according to their respective criteria.
1-4.illustrationAlt: Two voting criteria for the challenge phase

1-4.title: Place your stickers on the notes.
1-4.description: Drag a sticker onto a note. Select a sticker again or return it to the palette to withdraw your vote. Other members’ votes remain hidden while voting.

1-5.title: Discuss the results and choose one challenge as a team.
1-5.description: Use the votes as a reference. You do not have to choose the note with the most votes.
1-5.illustrationAlt: Discussing the notes and votes as a team

1-5.title: Select one note using “Choose a note to adopt.”
1-5.description: Select the button first, then choose a note on the board. Once the team has decided, use the button in the top-right to continue.
1-5.illustrationAlt: Selecting a note after entering adoption mode

2-1.title: Turn the challenge into a question about how to improve it.
2-1.description: Look at the selected challenge and ask, “How might we …?”
2-1.illustrationAlt: Turning a selected challenge into a question

2-1.title: Expand the question by substituting or removing something.
2-1.description: Example challenge: We often forget things.
2-1.illustrationAlt: Using SCAMPER prompts to reframe a challenge

2-2.title: Share your notes and learn what everyone thinks.
2-2.description: Take turns explaining your thoughts and gather ideas to work on as a team.
2-2.illustrationAlt: Team members sharing their sticky notes

2-2.title: Present when it is your turn, then hand over to the next person.
2-2.description: Check the presenter shown at the top of the screen. When it is your turn, drag your private notes onto the board and explain them. Select “Done!” when you finish to pass the turn.
2-2.illustrationAlt: Waiting for the previous presenter, sharing a note on your turn, then selecting Done

2-3.title: Vote for the questions you want to explore.
2-3.description: Use the two sticker types according to their respective criteria.
2-3.illustrationAlt: Two voting criteria for the question phase

2-3.title: Place your stickers on the notes.
2-3.description: Drag a sticker onto a note. Select a sticker again or return it to the palette to withdraw your vote. Other members’ votes remain hidden while voting.

2-4.title: Discuss the results and choose one question as a team.
2-4.description: Use the votes as a reference. You do not have to choose the question with the most votes.
2-4.illustrationAlt: Discussing the questions and votes as a team

2-4.title: Select one note using “Choose a note to adopt.”
2-4.description: Select the button first, then choose a note on the board. Once the team has decided, use the button in the top-right to continue.
2-4.illustrationAlt: Selecting a question after entering adoption mode

3-1.title: Write one solution to the selected question on each note.
3-1.description: Think freely about ways to make things better. Put one idea on each note.
3-1.illustrationAlt: Writing one solution on each sticky note

3-1.title: Use the question as a prompt for possible solutions.
3-1.description: Question: How might we check what we need without relying on memory?
3-1.illustrationAlt: Example of a solution to a question about remembering belongings

3-2.title: Share your notes and learn what everyone thinks.
3-2.description: Take turns explaining your thoughts and gather ideas to work on as a team.
3-2.illustrationAlt: Team members sharing their sticky notes

3-2.title: Present when it is your turn, then hand over to the next person.
3-2.description: Check the presenter shown at the top of the screen. When it is your turn, drag your private notes onto the board and explain them. Select “Done!” when you finish to pass the turn.
3-2.illustrationAlt: Waiting for the previous presenter, sharing a note on your turn, then selecting Done

3-3.title: Compare solutions by value and feasibility.
3-3.description: Discuss who benefits from each idea and how realistic it is to put into practice.
3-3.illustrationAlt: Comparing solutions by value and feasibility

3-3.title: Move the notes together and decide where they belong.
3-3.description: Place higher-value ideas toward the top and easier-to-implement ideas toward the right. You can adjust the positions from the previous sharing step.
3-3.illustrationAlt: Moving notes on a value and feasibility map

3-4.title: Vote for the solutions you want to work on.
3-4.description: Use the two sticker types according to their respective criteria.
3-4.illustrationAlt: Two voting criteria for the solution phase

3-4.title: Place your stickers on the notes.
3-4.description: Drag a sticker onto a note. Select a sticker again or return it to the palette to withdraw your vote. Other members’ votes remain hidden while voting.

3-5.title: Discuss the results and choose one solution as a team.
3-5.description: Use the votes and the map as references when deciding which solution to pursue.
3-5.illustrationAlt: Discussing the solutions and votes as a team

3-5.title: Select one note using “Choose a note to adopt.”
3-5.description: Select the button first, then choose a note on the board. Once the team has decided, use “Complete and view results” in the top-right to finish.
3-5.illustrationAlt: Selecting a solution after entering adoption mode

ideaSupportPanel.description: Choose one perspective that interests you and apply it to the question you decided on. Write any ideas that come to mind on sticky notes.

prompts.p1: Could it be used for another purpose?
prompts.p3: Could we change its shape, structure, or method?
prompts.p4: Could making it bigger create new value?
prompts.p5: Could making it smaller make it easier to use?
prompts.p7: Could reversing it lead to a new idea?

prompts.p1: Substitute: Can we replace it with something else?
prompts.p2: Combine: Can we combine it with other elements?
prompts.p3: Adapt: Can we borrow an approach from another context?
prompts.p4: Modify: Can we change its form or structure?
prompts.p5: Put to another use: Can we use it for a different purpose?
prompts.p6: Eliminate: Could it work without something?
prompts.p7: Reverse: Could we reverse the order or roles?

prompts.p1: Try imagining the opposite of the ideal state—a deliberately bad outcome.
prompts.p2: What would happen if we did the opposite of the usual approach?
prompts.p3: What if we reversed the roles of the people using and providing it?

prompts.p1: How does the food service industry solve similar challenges?
prompts.p2: How does the game industry make experiences fun and engaging?
prompts.p3: How does the hotel industry create comfortable experiences?
prompts.p4: How does the education industry support learning and understanding?
